Foundation examination: Volumes1–4Economics core examinationFinance core examinationGraduate qualifying sequenceIntegrated policy and investment caseResearch portfolioTeaching portfolioLeadership portfolio

Author-reviewed

Leadership portfolio

Defend a decision, show the work, bound the claim

Submit your own institutional strategy, resource and governance decisions, a people plan, a permitted crisis exercise and a retrospective on responsibility you actually held. An informed human must inspect the underlying records and evaluate your conduct within a stated scope. Solving the library's cases does not supply that experience.

Prerequisites are accounting, corporate finance, institutional risk, research, teaching and institutional leadership. The Volume18 project supplies a complete synthetic rehearsal. This cross-assessment requires an actual submission, permitted observation and a defense. The three fictional calibration dossiers below teach assessors how to distinguish correct analysis, observed work, consequential errors and appropriately limited readiness.

Demonstrate analytical breadth in academic and financial settings through your own complete cases or actual records. Actual observed responsibility may be in one appropriately bounded setting: for example, coordinating a permitted teaching-material project, an analytical service or a small operational improvement. Do not infer experience in the other setting. No exercise grants authority over money, people, sensitive information or institutional policy. Establish that authority through the actual organization before acting. Narrow, verifiable responsibility is preferable to an unsupported senior title.

1. What an assessor can conclude

A strategy may be reasoned but unaffordable; a budget may reconcile but lack authority; an authorized plan may never be executed; a delivered project may have no credible causal effect estimate. Treat those as distinct propositions. Use five domains: strategy and economic reasoning; resources and risk; governance and integrity; people and communication; execution, evidence and reflection. For each assign supported within scope, revision required, or not yet evaluable, with the exact evidence and limitation. These are qualitative judgments, not percentages to average.

Advance to a specifically described next responsibility only when the required actual-work evidence exists, the substantive arguments withstand review and every material objection affecting that responsibility is resolved. A missing observation is not a weak score that polished prose can offset. Fabricated work, false attribution, an unreconciled material resource account or an unresolved authority breach prevents the affected conclusion. A repaired breach remains in the history. An assessor may support model reasoning while withholding a claim of observed leadership. “Not yet evaluable” describes missing evidence or expertise; “revision required” identifies an evidenced defect.

For every claim keep a chain from original mandate to decision, authorization, action, output, acceptance and outcome. Record who did each part, which documents are contemporaneous, what was reconstructed later, and whose assistance was used. Identify an outcome's denominator and missing observations. An observed improvement does not identify your personal causal contribution without a credible alternative-outcome argument. A colleague's favorable report supplies observations within their access; it cannot reveal an unobserved counterfactual.

2. Six complete artifact groups

G1 — Strategy and the alternatives rejected

Submit a complete memo specifying institutional purpose, stakeholders, scope, success criteria, available options and the proposed allocation. State the objective separately from legal, ethical, resource and authority constraints. Derive the economic mechanism, opportunity cost and at least one meaningful changed-input decision. Include a defensible alternative that loses under the stated criterion and explain what would reverse the ranking. Supply the complete underlying data/model or documentary evidence, its provenance, uncertainty and source access. A slogan and a list of priorities are insufficient. The academic argument must protect credible scholarship and educational standards; the financial argument must connect business purpose with funded risk capacity. Clearly label supplied simulation assumptions and actual observations.

G2 — Original, revised and actual resources

Submit opening balances and restrictions, an operating and capital budget as relevant, a dated cash schedule, a downside scenario and the actual resource reconciliation for the real assignment. Distinguish cash, expense, assets, liabilities, equity, commitments and contingent receipts. Show every material resource owner, approval limit and funding dependency. Retain original baseline, approved revisions and actual costs/dates instead of moving the baseline to erase a miss. Explain forecast versus realized discrepancies. For the financial analytical case, reconcile a full balance sheet and liquidity/capital consequences; for the academic case, reconcile staff time, restricted funding and research/teaching commitments. Include assumptions and a complete computation that another reader can reproduce using supplied inputs.

G3 — Authority and accountability

Provide a governance map naming who proposes, authorizes, executes, checks and escalates each material decision. Attach the actual permitted mandate or an authorized verifier's scoped confirmation, including dates, limits, conflicts and material changes. Identify unresolved policy or legal questions for appropriately qualified local review; do not substitute this book's fictional rules. Distinguish recommendation, valid approval and execution. Show how a contested or failed decision was preserved, reviewed and resolved, or explicitly state that no such event occurred and demonstrate a clearly labeled hypothetical response. Record who can stop the action and what happens while evidence is incomplete.

G4 — Hiring, incentives and development

Submit a complete role/selection and incentive design appropriate to the proposed institution: job-related criteria, evidence to collect, consistent evaluation, conflicts, decision rights, pay or workload assumptions, likely behavioral response, unintended incentives, feedback and succession. If you have no authority to hire or set pay, label those documents analytical designs only. For your actual assignment show genuine delegation, coordination, feedback or development within authorized scope. Preserve the colleague's own response or an observer's event record where permitted; a manager's claim that coaching occurred is not equivalent. Explain what a metric misses and how an independent check or altered contract changes behavior. Do not infer general people-management competence from one pleasant meeting.

G5 — A permitted crisis exercise

Design and conduct an authorized tabletop or equivalent bounded exercise with an agreed facilitator or observer. Supply starting resources, successive evidence releases, available actions, deadlines, roles and constraints before the exercise. Preserve the participant's actual time-ordered decisions and messages before revealing later information. Provide the full benchmark analysis, including conditional probabilities or robust scenario reasoning where appropriate, liquidity/authority checks, alternatives and escalation. Distinguish exercise performance from a real emergency response. A solo written solution can evidence analysis but does not count as the independently observed exercise. Do not introduce a real operational disruption to create evidence.

G6 — Real responsibility, external review and continuation

Submit a complete retrospective on the actual assignment: the mandate, decision and action records, resources, accepted and rejected outputs, observed outcomes, team credit, failures, informed external-to-owner feedback, your response and the next evidence needed. Include at least one actual identifiable human reviewer with relevant access and competence, their relationship/conflicts, what they directly observed and what they could not judge. Supply the actual review text rather than an invented signature or paraphrased praise. An independent reviewer may be needed for contested specialized claims. The reviewer agreement and actual institution determine permissible access; the library promises neither confidentiality nor authorization. A proposed improvement remains proposed until its execution and later review are documented.

4. Review and defense procedure

First agree a realistic actual-work opportunity and the F1 scope. Before execution, establish the baseline, roles, observers and evidence access; approval is not retroactively created by a successful outcome. Next submit all six complete artifact groups and the full records behind their references. The coordinating assessor checks access and expertise, then assigns financial, economic/research and people/governance review as needed. One qualified person may cover multiple domains, but disclose relationships; authors do not become independent reviewers of their own work by changing roles.

Reviewers inspect the whole argument and reconstruct material calculations, compare original with revised/actual records, and examine adverse evidence. Conduct the permitted crisis exercise with unrevealed later releases and retain the real responses. Obtain the actual human observation of responsibility and feedback. Give the candidate a written opportunity to correct factual errors, respond to criticisms and identify unresolved disagreement. A correction to a document does not prove changed conduct. Where a dispute materially affects advancement, request another appropriately qualified reviewer with access to the relevant record. Preserve dissent and its reasons instead of averaging it away.

A proposed 60-minute defense uses 10 minutes for the integrated strategy, 15 for a resource/proof reconstruction, 15 for an unseen changed-input crisis or people decision, 10 for actual responsibility and team credit, and 10 for limitations and next work. This timing is an uncalibrated design choice. Questions must fit the agreed scope; record actual permitted aids, prompting and answers. A read-aloud prepared answer is not independent reconstruction. Assess the five domains separately, then state the precise next responsibility, conditions and excluded claims. Research originality and observed teaching require their own qualified judgments through the linked portfolios; this defense does not replace them.

5. Three original assessor-calibration dossiers

Every person, organization, date, signature described in words, outcome and reviewer statement in the next three cases is invented. “Observed” below means stipulated within that fiction. These are full calibration specimens, never evidence about the reader.

Case1 — correct institutional analysis without executed responsibility

Fictional Cedar Academic Center asks candidate Mira for a proposed one-term support program. Its mission score values accepted preparation outputs, not measured learning or publications. Each of three projects may be selected once or omitted, with no partial execution. The unrestricted budget is10 kCU after reserving all essential obligations; available staff capacity is8 blocks. No borrowing or overtime is allowed. A2 kCU grant has been promised solely for project A but has not been received and cannot fund a commitment under the stipulated local rule.

Complete option table: cost kCU, staff blocks, stipulated mission score
ProjectCostStaffScoreComplete intended output and acceptance
A649Research replication workshop: full data/provenance note, reproducible analysis and qualified methods review
B458Teaching tutorial: complete prerequisite task, lesson, independent transfer task/key and observed delivery if later authorized
C537Access and integrity clinic: verified reading access, source/assistance register and full practice corrections

Full candidate strategy, version1. “Select B and C. They cost9, use8 staff blocks and score15. Keep1 unrestricted unit uncommitted. A alone scores9; the seemingly attractive A+B needs9 blocks, and A+C costs11. Do not count the promised grant. The academic reviewer must inspect complete tasks and keys, the methods reviewer must assess any replication claim, and finance must confirm received funds before commitments. I will coordinate the work only after receiving authority; I have not delivered it.”

Governance and people plan. The fictional council would approve scope and resources; finance would verify payment authority; the academic lead would accept B, and an integrity reviewer C. Mira proposes assigning5 staff blocks to tutorial preparation/delivery and3 to the clinic, with acceptance before release. A job-related selection task asks a proposed tutor to explain an incorrect causal claim using supplied data and an original correction; two readers apply the same disclosed criteria before discussing scores. No hiring or assessment has actually occurred. There is no pay contract or promotion claim hidden in the mission score.

Record and complete review. On fictional Day1 Mira emails version1 and its complete option calculation. The council replies only “Received for discussion”; no approval, spending, delivery, candidate observation or student outcome follows. Reviewer Jo inspects the full memo/table on Day2 and writes: “I reproduced the feasible menu and agree with B+C under the supplied criterion. The plan correctly separates the promised grant and actual spendable budget. I reviewed analysis, not leadership conduct; I did not observe staff assignment, delivery or a crisis exercise. I work for the council and am external to Mira's authorship, not an accreditor. The score is stipulated, so neither the ranking nor my agreement proves educational impact.”

  1. Enumerate all feasible selections and prove the optimum. Recompute if the2 research-only grant is received before commitment, with all other facts unchanged. Issue a complete readiness disposition and candidate response without promoting a proposal into performed work.
Complete analysis and disposition

The eight subsets have(cost,staff,score): empty(0,0,0),A(6,4,9),B(4,5,8),C(5,3,7),AB(10,9,17),AC(11,7,16),BC(9,8,15),ABC(15,12,24). The feasible menu is empty,A,B,C,BC; its unique highest score is15 atBC. Enumerating every binary subset proves global optimality in this finite model. If the grant is actually received and may pay2 of A's cost, unrestricted cost is total cost−2 when A is selected and unchanged otherwise. AB still violates staff; AC now costs9 unrestricted, uses7 blocks and scores16; ABC remains infeasible. AC is then uniquely best, leaving1 unrestricted and0 grant cash, with1 staff block unused. B+C remains feasible but loses by1 score. Results(base cost,staff,score;received-grant cost,staff,score,unused staff) are ((9,8,15),(9,7,16,1)).

Assessor disposition: “Strategy and resource reasoning are supported within the supplied finite menu. Governance and people documents are inspectable designs; their implementation is not yet evaluable. Execution, crisis exercise and real responsibility are missing, so the actual-work portfolio is not ready. The receipt acknowledgment is not an approval. Preserve Jo's limited review, original option table and promised-grant status. Do not describe16 as an achieved institutional benefit.”

Candidate response: “My present evidence supports the analytical recommendation, not institutional leadership. I will request a bounded authorized coordination role, actual resource/acceptance owners and an informed observer before acting. If approval and received funding later change, I will issue a new dated release and recompute the selection; until then BC remains the funded proposal. I will retain actual task assignments, costs, delivered artifacts, rejection/acceptance and feedback, and conduct the separately authorized exercise. Missing opportunities remain pending.” Full credit requires the exhaustive feasibility proof and a decision about actual evidence, not simply an excellent numerical score.

Case2 — real-in-fiction delivery with a material authority and liquidity failure

Fictional Rowan Analytics is a service company, not a stipulated regulated bank. Project owner Eli receives authority to implement a reporting tool at a total vendor commitment of8 kCU, with no change-order authority. Opening cash18 plus other assets82 equals liabilities85 plus equity15. The invented board policy requires cash at least6 at every recorded event. Accounts payable5, already included in the85 liabilities, must be settled on Day2. It was available in the original records but Eli omitted it from the cash forecast. All numbers are kCU; no tax, interest, depreciation or other transaction occurs.

Actual-in-fiction events. Day1: Eli pays the authorized vendor8 in advance for future services. Record a prepaid asset8, not an immediate expense; no service is yet accepted. Day2: the controller pays the existing payable5. Day3: the acceptance reviewer confirms3 of vendor services consumed and accepted, leaving5 prepaid. Day4: Eli orders and pays an extra2 integration expense without approval; that work is performed and cannot be reversed for a refund. All payments and the accepted service are recorded. Day5: the sponsor agrees to seek an equity contribution3. Day6: no contribution has arrived. There is no actual cash receipt hidden in the agreement.

Full financial review, controller Fen. “I inspected all five entries and the bank records through Day6. Cash is3, not6; the promised contribution is absent. Paying a recognized payable still reduces cash and the liability. The advance was initially an asset exchange; consumption3 later reduces the prepaid asset and equity. The floor was already breached at Day2, before the unapproved integration. I reconcile accounting, not technical completion. I work for the company and did not approve Eli's change order. Preserve the breach dates rather than treating later possible funding as a cure that occurred earlier.”

Full delivery and people review, technical lead Gia. “I accepted the3 service portion on Day3, not the entire8 advance. Analyst Hal prepared the mapping and technician Ira executed the connection; Eli coordinated instructions. The extra integration ran on Day4 but bypassed the authorized change process. I saw Eli tell Hal to mark the remaining service complete because the invoice was paid; Hal refused and retained my acceptance record. I require a corrected status report and a changed checkpoint before another release. I cannot conclude that Eli improved customer outcomes, which were not measured.”

  1. Reconstruct every balance sheet and cash-floor breach. Derive the minimum actual equity receipt needed to restore the floor after Day4, and compare a counterfactual staged vendor advance5 with unchanged service consumption and extra expense. Write a complete correction, immediate control response and assessor disposition. Distinguish an authorized future repair from an executed repair and from erasing the earlier breach.
Complete ledger, repair and judgment

Write each row(cash,prepaid,other assets,liabilities,equity). Opening is(18,0,82,85,15); after Day1(10,8,82,85,15); Day2(5,8,82,80,15); Day3(5,5,82,80,12); Day4 and Day6(3,5,82,80,10). Assets equal liabilities plus equity in every row. The cash floor6 is met on Day1, missed by1 on Day2/3 and by3 on Day4/6. The agreement on Day5 changes none of these balances. Results are ((18,0,82,85,15),(10,8,82,85,15),(5,8,82,80,15),(5,5,82,80,12),(3,5,82,80,10)).

An actual cash equity contribution e≥0 gives closing cash3+e and equity10+e, with other accounts unchanged. Restoring cash≥6 requires e≥3; e3 attains the bound and yields(6,5,82,80,13), assets93. This is the minimum within the specified equity-only repair; borrowing or refunds were not supplied as options. If funds are never received, the repair remains unexecuted. Later receipt cannot change the earlier breach dates or authorize the extra2 retrospectively.

Under the separate counterfactual of an originally agreed staged vendor advance5, Day1 cash13/prepaid5, Day2 cash8/liabilities80, Day3 prepaid2/equity12, Day4 cash6/equity10. Final(6,2,82,80,10) balances assets90. The floor holds throughout this altered payment schedule. The total vendor commitment may still be8, leaving3 due later; include that future obligation in the forward cash plan rather than declare a permanent saving. The extra2 remains unauthorized. This illustrates a feasible cash-timing alternative under an additional agreement, not evidence that the actual vendor offered it. Results(minimum receipt,repaired row,staged row,unpaid original commitment) are (3,(6,5,82,80,13),(6,2,82,80,10),3).

Corrected report: “Withdraw E1's completion, funding and sole-value claims. Actual cash is3 and the remaining prepaid service5 has not been accepted. Day2 first breached the6 cash floor; Day4's unapproved2 payment worsened the gap. The actual service expense3 and extra2 leave equity10; the original advance alone was not expense8. Fen reconciled the entries; Gia accepted only the specified service; Hal and Ira supplied the technical work. Proposed equity3 has not arrived, so it cannot be booked or used to release more commitments. Preserve E1, the source entries and this correction.”

Control response: “Escalate the current3 cash shortfall and unauthorized change to the sponsor/controller through the supplied process; stop further discretionary commitments pending valid approval and verified resources. Keep the outstanding vendor obligation and acceptance status visible. The sponsor must choose a permitted actual funding or scope/payment response; do not fabricate a receipt. Require an independently reconciled cash schedule including existing liabilities, a separate acceptance sign-off and written change authorization before the next release. Protect Hal's accurate report rather than reward completion counts.”

Disposition: “Execution occurred within this fiction, but resources, authority and integrity of the original report require revision and reassessment. The corrected calculation can support learning; it does not yet show changed conduct. Do not extend financial discretion. Request the actual corrected communication, a resolved funding plan and an observed next checkpoint with independent cash/acceptance review. Preserve the original breach, contribution credits and reviewer scopes. No single favorable delivery item compensates for these material defects.” Full credit requires all dated ledger states, actual versus promised funding, full correction and a bounded decision rather than the label ‘bad leader.’

Case3 — a bounded observed coordination improvement

Fictional Elm Methods Service gives owner Noor an eight-hour scheduling responsibility for two consenting staff members, A and B, each limited to4 paid hours. The task is to prepare two streams of accepted work, X and Y, before handover. Their targets are8 and6 units. Rates are stipulated deterministic planning quantities: A produces3 X or1 Y per hour; B produces1 X or2 Y. Effort is divisible, switching has no cost, all output is checked, and no staff member works both tasks in the same hour. The only objective is to maximize the smaller target ratio z=min(X/8,Y/6). This is an invented service metric, not research quality or staff worth.

Let t be A's hours on X and u B's hours on X. With all remaining paid hours assigned to Y, 0≤t,u≤4, X=3t+u and Y=12−t−2u. Using all hours is without loss here because each available hour increases some nonnegative output and no cost beyond the fixed paid capacity enters the objective. A real institution would need to validate rates, switching and work quality rather than importing them.

Actual-in-fiction first release and observations. Day1 Noor assigns A four hours to X and B four to Y. Both staff agree to the stated hours; reviewer Pia checks the complete work and accepts X12,Y8. All8 paid hours cost1 kCU per hour, exactly the authorized8. There is no unpaid work or restricted grant. Noor initially writes “Both exceeded target, therefore no feasible schedule can improve balance.” Staff member B asks whether a small amount of A's time on Y would improve the weaker ratio. Noor records the question rather than treating it as resistance.

Actual-in-fiction feedback and revised release. Pia writes on Day2: “I checked accepted quantities and observed the scheduling discussion. The first schedule delivers within hours and budget, but the optimality claim needs a proof. I saw B propose the trade-off and Noor ask both staff to check it. I am an operations reviewer, not an independent evaluator of educational impact. Inspect the full rate assumptions and preserve the earlier schedule.” Noor derives the bound below, credits B's question and shares a revised schedule with both staff. On Day3 they execute that schedule in a second stipulated comparable eight-hour work period; Pia directly checks the fractional service units and accepts the quantities. These invented divisible quantities make the model exact; actual work might be indivisible.

Complete governance, people and crisis record. The sponsor authorized one8 kCU period on each of Day1 and Day3 before execution, with no transfer of hours between staff and no authority to change pay. Noor had scheduling authority only. The two signed-in-fiction attendance records show4 hours for each staff member in each period; total cost across the two periods is16, within the separately approved16. On Day2 an agreed observer runs a short tabletop: “B is now available only3 hours; use the same objective and rates.” Noor pauses the planned release, recomputes the response below and tells the sponsor that the original schedule cannot be promised. No staff absence or actual service disruption occurs; this is an observed exercise inside the fiction.

Full final reviewer statement. Pia writes: “I inspected the rate table, both complete schedules, all accepted quantities, the16 cost ledger, the preexisting two-period authorizations and the exercise response. I observed Noor receive B's challenge without suppressing it, check the trade-off with A and B, and issue the revised schedule before Day3. The bounded coordination and response to criticism are evidenced. I did not evaluate hiring, promotion, original research, classroom teaching, crisis management in an actual emergency or durable staff development. I am employed by the sponsor but did not author the schedules. The two periods do not identify a general causal effect of Noor's leadership; rates and comparability are stipulated in this calibration.”

  1. Prove the globally optimal schedule and uniqueness under the stated criterion. Reconcile the first and revised output ratios and paid resources. Solve the observed exercise with B limited to3 hours, and a separate transfer with both targets6 and original4/4 hours. Issue a complete scoped readiness decision and candidate retrospective.
Full proof, changed schedules and scoped judgment

For any feasible t,u, X+3Y=36−5u≤36. Attaining ratio z requires X≥8z,Y≥6z, hence26z≤36 and z≤18/13. Choose u0,t48/13: X144/13,Y108/13, with A's remaining4/13 hours and B's4 hours assigned to Y. Both ratios equal18/13 and the bound is attained. Equality in the bound forces u0; equality in the sum of target requirements forces both target ratios equal, so t48/13 is unique. The first schedule has X12,Y8, ratios3/2 and4/3, minimum4/3. Its gap from the optimum is18/13−4/3=2/39. Each period uses8 paid hours, costs8 and meets its own approval. Results(first outputs/ratios/minimum;optimal t,u,X,Y,z;improvement) are ((12,8,3/2,4/3,4/3),(48/13,0,144/13,108/13,18/13),2/39).

With B limited to3 hours, Y=(4−t)+2(3−u)=10−t−2u. Therefore X+3Y=30−5u≤30, so z≤15/13. Set u0,t40/13; X120/13,Y90/13, both attaining15/13, with A's Y time12/13 and B's Y time3. Total hours7, cost7 if the same1-per-hour charge applies; do not bill8 executed hours or promise the original output. The original two-period actual ledger remains16 because this absence is only an exercise. Under the separate targets6/6 with original hours, the bound is24z≤36, so z≤3/2. Set u0,t3, giving X9,Y9 and A's Y time1. Both bounds are attained and unique by the same equality argument. Results(exercise t,u,X,Y,z,hours;new-target t,u,X,Y,z) are ((40/13,0,120/13,90/13,15/13,7),(3,0,9,9,3/2)).

Assessor disposition: “Advance within the bounded scope of another comparable scheduling/coordination assignment, with the same independent acceptance and resource checks. Strategy and resources are supported by the full proof and actual-in-fiction reconciled periods. Governance is supported within the preauthorized16 and scheduling-only mandate. People/communication evidence includes receiving, crediting and using B's challenge. Execution/reflection includes an issued correction and a later observed revised schedule. The permitted tabletop supports response to that changed capacity; it does not certify real emergency leadership. Hiring, financial custody, research originality, teaching delivery and broad institutional leadership remain unobserved.”

Candidate retrospective: “My first schedule was feasible but my optimality claim was wrong. B identified the missing trade-off; I derived and checked the corrected schedule with both staff and credited their contributions. Pia observed execution and accepted the outputs; neither her record nor the stipulated rates identifies my personal causal impact. I kept the original release, actual16 cost and separate exercise status. For a next comparable role I will state the objective and prove the resource bound before claiming optimality. Wider responsibility needs new authority, appropriate domain expertise and independent observation of that work.” Full credit requires the equality-based uniqueness proof, complete changed schedules and a specific readiness boundary, not universal praise.

6. Six defense challenges and complete calibration answers

These questions calibrate the protocol. Actual assessors must choose an unseen variation appropriate to the candidate's own submitted work and record the real response on F6. A candidate's reading of these printed answers is not a completed defense.

  1. In Cedar, the unrestricted budget becomes11 with original8 staff blocks and no received grant. Is the old choice still optimal? Explain the opportunity cost and authority requirement.
  2. In Rowan, suppose a verified actual equity receipt2 arrives after Day6. Reconcile the new balance sheet, remaining floor gap and authority status.
  3. For Elm's original resources, a candidate reports only X12 and omits Y. Can you certify balanced performance or global optimality? State exactly what additional evidence and proof are required.
  4. A reviewer praises an owner's project profit but has not inspected the original benchmark or team contributions. Write a bounded response and identify the missing causal comparison.
  5. An owner offers an invitation to a crisis observer and a complete answer key as evidence that the exercise occurred. What status and next step follow?
  6. A candidate has the full Elm-type observed record but no real academic teaching or financial custody. Write the next-responsibility decision and explain how to extend evidence without inventing authority.
Full defense answer guides

D1 — a binding resource changes

AC now costs11 and uses7 blocks, so it is feasible and scores16, exceedingBC15. AB still violates the8-block staff limit; ABC violates both. Exhausting the unchanged eight subsets proves AC uniquely optimal. It leaves0 of the new unrestricted budget and1 staff block, with no grant. The extra unit of available budget raises the finite menu's best score by1, but is not a universal marginal return or observed educational benefit. Before acting, obtain the actual authorization for11 and revise the release; a hypothetical budget change does not supply cash. Result(cost,staff,score,unused staff) is (11,7,16,1).

D2 — an incomplete repair

Starting from(3,5,82,80,10), actual equity2 gives(5,5,82,80,12), assets92. The6 cash floor still lacks1. Result(row,gap) is ((5,5,82,80,12),1). Record the actual receipt once, with its identifier and date. Neither receipt nor remaining promise authorizes the original extra2 or changes the Day2 breach. Continue the actual permitted resolution and withhold unfunded commitments; do not label a partly funded plan restored.

D3 — the omitted mission matters

X12 alone does not establish min(X/8,Y/6); Y could be below target or unobserved. Request accepted Y quantities, actual hours and assignments for both staff, complete costs and authority, then compare both ratios. For the given deterministic model the full proof uses X+3Y≤36 and attainment at(t,u)=(48/13,0), not a claim that exceeding X's target proves optimality. In an actual setting, inspect the rate and acceptance assumptions rather than assume the model is empirically correct. Preserve the partial report as incomplete evidence.

D4 — praise has a perimeter

“Thank you for the observed facts; retain their dates and scope. Please inspect opening resources, the predeclared comparison, all costs and the actual contribution record before concluding relative success. Profit may be positive while trailing a suitable benchmark. Even a reconciled comparison does not identify the outcome under a specified alternative owner/team process, so it does not isolate my personal effect. Credit each contributor and identify the unseen counterfactual. Your review can support the inspected observation while leaving causal attribution and future skill unresolved.” A complete answer distinguishes an arithmetic comparator from an intervention replacing the leader; it does not invent the replacement outcome.

D5 — preparation is not observation

Status: exercise designed, observer invited, agreement and execution not observed. Inspect the full releases/key as design evidence, but do not fill in an attendance or success field. Secure actual permission and observer agreement, conduct the bounded exercise with later releases initially hidden, retain time-ordered real decisions/messages and the observer's own scoped review, then assess and respond. If the opportunity is unavailable, keep the gate pending. A rehearsal must not create a real disruption merely to satisfy this protocol.

D6 — scoped advancement and a real next step

“Advance to another comparable scheduling/coordination assignment under explicit authority, resource ceilings and independent acceptance. The observed correction and response to B's challenge support that scope. Academic teaching, financial custody and broad institutional leadership remain untested. To extend the claim, agree an appropriately bounded actual role, qualified observers and permitted records in the new domain before acting. Submit the substantive work, actual feedback and a later response; use the research and teaching portfolios for their distinct requirements. Do not take control of funds or people on the strength of this book's recommendation.” The next step must name both the new evidence and its authority, not guarantee an appointment.

8. A complete continuation decision

After the actual defense, issue a dated report naming the exact release reviewed, real assessors, evidence access, five domain judgments, material disagreements and scope of any advancement. The candidate responds in writing, retains original versions and defines a next task that tests the largest remaining weakness. Agree the authority, observer, resources and review date before the new work. At that review inspect what actually occurred rather than counting a calendar interval as progress. If opportunity, access or reviewer expertise is absent, record the blocked claim and choose a permissible narrower task.

A complete candidate statement may read: “My present record supports the named analytical and observed coordination tasks. It does not establish every research frontier, effective teaching at all levels or broad financial authority. My next agreed task will address the specified weakness, with an actual owner, resource limit, output and informed human review. I will preserve adverse evidence, assistance and uncertainty, and revise the claim if the record changes.” Replace that statement with the actual facts of your submission. Do not submit it as evidence of work by itself.

Sources and scope

The measurement distinction between accepted work and incurred cost is supported by the bounded DOE earned-value overview inspected for Chapter11. Distinguishing measurement, comparison and appraisal follows the bounded public CFA portfolio-evaluation summary inspected there; no full restricted reading or professional certification is claimed. The distinction between capital and available liquidity is explained in the retained Bank of England capital and liquidity primer. All three calibration models, fictional rules, records, reviewer statements, proofs, forms and judgments here are original. They impose no jurisdiction-specific law and supply no actual learner observation. Independent qualified human evaluation and experience remain essential.
